A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HydraFake dataset and Veritas research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original HydraFake evaluations, training-stage and reward ablations, reasoning-quality assessments and robustness experiments in Section 5 and Appendix A.4.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds specialized-detector comparisons, external benchmark evaluations, component ablations, efficiency measurements and failure analyses.

M1.justification: The pattern-aware SFT, MiPO cold-start and P-GRPO pipeline, including its losses and reward components, remains unchanged in Section 4. Additional annotation and prompt descriptions document the existing method; restricted-data and reward-model experiments do not establish a revised proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 Tables 14–15 add AIGIBench facial subsets, LOKI, FakeClue, Forensics-Bench and Nano-banana-150K evaluations. Coverage expands beyond HydraFake facial images to general synthetic imagery, including animals, documents, satellite images and scenes illustrated in Figures 23–27. AIGIBench also supplies data for an additional P-GRPO training experiment.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 adds evaluated specialized MLLM detectors: M2F2-Det, FakeShield, SIDA-7B, SIDA-13B, FFAA and FakeVLM. These constitute a substantial new comparator category; the original ten vision detectors and six generic MLLMs remain. New qualitative comparisons also examine these specialized detectors.

E3.justification: New protocols include restricted-source VERITAS-MINI with OOD-only averaging, equal-sized 48K FF++ versus HydraFake training comparisons, AIGIBench facial evaluation using VFHQ real images, F1 reporting and batched latency measurements. The reported IC-Light sample count changes from 1,676 in v1 Table 7 to 2,082 in v2 Table 9. MiMo prompting is now explicitly described as omitting prior knowledge. These reporting changes do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds individual reasoning-pattern removals, separate MiPO rejection-type ablations, data-selection experiments, KL-penalty and rollout-count sensitivity, and reward-model comparisons (Tables 5–6 and 17–19; Figure 10). It also adds efficiency analyses and explicit failure and comparative case studies. The original training-stage, reasoning-quality and JPEG/blur analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v2 Table 19 newly identifies two random data-sampling settings with seeds 42 and 100. This adds limited seed-specific reporting, without introducing confidence intervals, significance tests or aggregated training-run variability, or establishing an increased repeated-run budget.

E6.justification: Original performance-table entries remain unchanged, including Veritas's 90.7% average in Table 1. Substantial new results include VERITAS-MINI's 85.8% OOD average, 88.9% accuracy on the AIGIBench evaluation and 72.1% on LOKI, alongside new ablation, timing and qualitative findings. These are additional results under newly reported conditions, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The objectives and reward definitions in Equations 1–6 and the explanation-versus-reasoning formulations in Equations 7–8 are retained. v2 adds conceptual explanations but no new or substantively revised formal assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The headline dataset, two-stage method and OOD-generalization contributions remain unchanged. The limited narrowing is that Section 2.2 removes v1's explicit 'first attempt' priority claim for introducing human-like reasoning into deepfake detection. Additional experiments principally support the retained contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of individual reasoning patterns, MiPO rejection types, exploration strength, group size and inference-cost tradeoffs. It explains its disagreement with BusterX++ about cold-start training and adds an explicit image-only benchmark limitation and discussion of video detection challenges. Failure analysis extends the discussion beyond v1's existing low-resolution caveat.

D1.justification: Appendix A.2 newly documents GPU resources, stage-specific training times, software frameworks, baseline preprocessing, augmentation, training budgets and validation selection. Appendices A.4/A.6 add real-image annotation procedures, expanded artifact definitions, valid output formats and training/inference prompts. These substantially improve documentation, although Figure 40's displayed system prompt conflicts with its caption's default-system description.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including DFBench, BusterX/BusterX++, LOKI, SophiaVL-R1, DeepfakeBench and Swift, and explicitly contrasts its cold-start findings with BusterX++. It also removes the 'first attempt' wording. The main related-work organization and positioning around pattern-aware reasoning versus post-hoc explanations remain intact.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose and section ordering are retained. v2 makes localized edits to the abstract, related work and conclusion, shortens HydraFake-100K to HydraFake in the narrative, updates author/header information, and adds an appendix contents guide and subsections. The scientific additions do not amount to a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: Table 1 is expanded and grouped by model category. v2 adds numerous ablation, benchmark and efficiency displays, comparative reasoning panels, failure examples and prompt panels. v1 Figure 4 is relocated and expanded as v2 Figure 9; the original training-stage charts and reasoning-quality/robustness tables are retained under new numbers.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation beyond v1's HydraFake-centered evidence: specialized MLLM comparisons with a restricted-training control, external benchmark testing, and targeted component ablations address important gaps in assessing generalization and the proposed mechanisms. Detailed implementation information and explicit failure and modality limitations also improve reproducibility and interpretation. The original scores remain unchanged, and Figure 40 introduces a prompt-documentation inconsistency, but this localized ambiguity does not outweigh the substantial gains in evidential support and transparency.
